findings.message: The docstring says this is terminal and the task should "fail fast instead of burning retries", but a plain RuntimeError does not stop Airflow retrying: a task with retries=3 will re-run the whole agent loop three times on bad credentials. If fail-fast is the intent it needs to derive from AirflowFailException (or the base class must translate it), otherwise the contract documented here and in toolsets.rst is not what actually happens.

timeout is accepted, documented as "Seconds to wait for a single invocation", and then never used - nothing in invoke(), call_tool() or the tool definition applies it, so a caller who passes timeout=30 gets no timeout at all. Either enforce it here (asyncio.wait_for around invoke, with the thread caveat documented) or drop it from the base signature rather than leaving subclasses to reach into a private _timeout.

asyncio.to_thread uses the loop's default executor, which is capped at min(32, cpu_count+4) and shared with everything else in the worker process. Combined with sequential=False and the documented fact that an abandoned invoke_sync keeps its thread until the vendor call returns, a handful of minute-long agent calls can starve every other to_thread user. Worth a dedicated bounded executor, or at least a concurrency limit per toolset.

The comment two lines up says the counters are tagged by platform "to keep cardinality bounded", but tool is the Dag author's tool_name, which is unbounded across a deployment - that is the cardinality problem the comment claims to avoid. The tag set also disagrees with the table in toolsets.rst, which lists only from_platform/to_platform and platform/role; please reconcile the two (and the metrics_template.yaml entry) whichever way you land.
